findings.title: Strengthened Regex Anchors for Header Validation
findings.description:
The regular expression for validating header names and values has been changed to explicitly anchor to the end of the string using `\Z` instead of `$`. In Python's `re` module, `$` matches before a trailing newline, allowing strings like `foo
` or `bar
` to potentially pass validation if not handled carefully, although the character class `[^
]` already excludes them. The addition of `\Z` provides a stricter, more correct anchor for byte strings, preventing subtle validation bypasses related to trailing newlines in binary header data. This is a defense-in-depth improvement against HTTP Request Smuggling or Header Injection via malformed header names/values.
findings.suggestion: This change is correct and improves security. No action required. The addition of `\Z` ensures that the regex does not match patterns that have a trailing newline before the end of the string, which is crucial for strict header validation in low-level network libraries.
